findings.title: Backup code login does not verify password in the 2FA step (password check is skipped when only backupCode is provided? / used-code reuse)
findings.body: Used backup codes are set to null in the array, but the check `backupCodes.indexOf(code)` is a non-atomic read-modify-write. Two concurrent logins with the same code can both succeed before the update lands, so a single-use code can be used more than once. Also, when all codes are consumed the array stays full of nulls and nothing tells the user.

findings.title: Backup code comparison is non-constant-time and user input is not type/length validated
findings.body: `indexOf` on plaintext codes is a non-constant-time compare. `credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` also assumes a string. Only the shared generic rate limit applies, which is weak protection for a 40-bit code. Codes are never validated against format before comparison.

findings.title: Disable endpoint crashes on non-string backupCode and null-valued entries are not handled
findings.body: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll` throws a 500 if backupCode is not a string (e.g. a number or object in the JSON body). Unlike login, no rate limiting is applied to this endpoint, so backup codes can be guessed by an authenticated session holder. Also, `symmetricDecrypt` and `JSON.parse` are not guarded.

findings.title: Backup codes regenerated and returned on every setup call, and stored/validated without being consumed on the null entries
findings.body: Each call to setup (including abandoned setups) overwrites existing backupCodes and returns them in plaintext. The codes are persisted before the user confirms TOTP, so an abandoned setup leaves codes in the DB while twoFactorEnabled is false. Combined with the login check, any user whose setup was abandoned has stale codes if they later enable 2FA via another route.

findings.title: Blob URL leaks and cancel/close do not clear sensitive backup codes from state
findings.body: `backupCodesUrl` in the handler closure is stale (revokes only the value from the render), and the object URL is never revoked when the modal closes. Backup codes remain in component state after `resetState`, which does not clear `backupCodes`, `dataUri`, `secret` or `backupCodesUrl`. Closing via the dialog's onOpenChange also bypasses resetState, so reopening the modal could resume at the backup-codes step.

findings.title: Lost-access toggle button lacks type="button" and resetForm clears values rather than unregistering
findings.body: The 'lost access' Button is inside a form and has no explicit `type="button"`; depending on the Button default it may submit the form. Also when switching to the BackupCode input, `required` and minLength validation on the hidden TOTP vs backup field combine with `setValue` resets, and a stale `totpCode`/`backupCode` can be sent together; the server prefers backupCode if truthy.

findings.title: Component misnamed TwoFactor
findings.body: The default export in BackupCode.tsx is named `TwoFactor`, duplicating the name of the other component and making stack traces/devtools confusing.

findings.title: Backup code errors surfaced but lost-access state not reset on 2FA return, and email-login totp path not handled
findings.body: For the external TOTP flow (`totpEmail`), the lost-access footer is not shown (ExternalTotpFooter), so users who authenticated via Google/SAML cannot use backup codes. Additionally, the authorize path skips password verification only when `totpCode` is present; for a backup-code submission with password the flow works, but for IdP users `!credentials.totpCode` is true and they get ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled.

findings.title: No tests for backup code login or disable with backup code
findings.body: The security-sensitive backup code paths (login, single-use enforcement, disable) are untested; the PR only adds UI download/copy checks and leaves a TODO. The PR description acknowledges no tests were added.
